claims.text: The initial substrate is a pure Cu matrix.
A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy film can adhere to a Cu matrix surface.
The RHEA film has excellent interface properties.
The RHEA film's interface properties cause its adhesion to the Cu matrix.
Depositing the nanocrystalline RHEA film enhances the wear resistance of the Cu matrix.
The film is deposited at room temperature.
The film is deposited at atmospheric pressure.
The RHEA film thickness is between 1 and 5 micrometers.
The film–Cu interface is the structural mediator governing adhesion and wear performance.
The high-entropy nature of the nanocrystalline RHEA improves its interface properties.
The refractory nature of the nanocrystalline RHEA improves its interface properties.
Strong film adhesion causes improved wear resistance.
The coated Cu matrix will exhibit at least 30% greater wear resistance than bare Cu, as evaluated from volume loss per unit sliding distance.
Wear performance will be compared against a bare, uncoated Cu matrix.
The wear response can be evaluated using a ball-on-disk sliding test that measures volume loss per unit distance and coefficient of friction.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 30% improvement, and the falsification rule initially says failure to reach 30% falsifies the hypothesis, but it then says the hypothesis is rejected only below 20%. Results from 20% to less than 30% therefore have contradictory or indeterminate status.
